pages.title: About Shisei Clinic
pages.content:
About Shisei Clinic

Founded in 2015, Shisei Clinic provides unhurried chiropractic care, soft-tissue therapy, and movement coaching for people who sit all week.

ABOUT

Since 2015

Since 2015

Shisei Clinic was established in 2015 to support people who spend forty hours a week sitting at screens. Modern office work concentrates mechanical load into the neck, shoulders, and lower spine, yet traditional clinical visits often feel rushed and impersonal. Located in Suite 204 at 1180 Linden Row in Vancouver, our clinic features three treatment rooms and one dedicated movement room designed for quiet, focused care. We reserve a full sixty minutes for every initial consultation so that we have ample time to listen to your history, assess joint mobility, and explain what we observe.

What We Do Not Do

We believe clinical care should remain grounded, transparent, and respectful of your autonomy. We never pressure patients into purchasing extensive prepaid treatment packages or locking themselves into rigid long-term contracts. In addition, we do not take routine X-rays in our clinic. Diagnostic imaging is only recommended when clinical examination reveals specific red flags, in which case we coordinate directly with medical physicians. Our clinical recommendations focus entirely on helping your spine adapt comfortably to your working routine, with treatment schedules that adapt to your personal progress rather than an arbitrary sales quota.

Our Principles

Our practice operates on three straightforward principles: clinical thoroughness, clear communication, and practical self-care. First, thoroughness means we examine how your whole body moves before initiating any physical adjustment. Second, clear communication ensures you understand the purpose of every manual technique we apply and every movement we recommend. Third, practical self-care means our clinicians provide realistic desk adjustments and simple postural drills that fit smoothly into busy working days. We aim to help you build resilient movement patterns that keep your neck, back, and shoulders feeling comfortable long after you leave our rooms.

Questions first? Call +1 604 555 0142 or write to hello@shisei.example. Reception is open six days a week.

pages.title: Conditions We Care For
pages.content:
Conditions We Care For

We evaluate and care for joint stiffness, muscle strain, and postural fatigue caused by prolonged sitting and repetitive screen work.

CONDITIONS

WHAT WE SEE

Three concerns, and what else we see

NECK & SHOULDERS

Neck and Shoulder Tension

Holding your head forward while staring at monitors places substantial strain on the cervical spine and the upper trapezius muscles. Over forty hours of weekly desk work, this sustained muscular contraction can cause persistent stiffness, limited rotation, and uncomfortable tightness across the tops of both shoulders. Our chiropractors evaluate segmental joint motion in the cervical and thoracic spine, using precise manual adjustments and gentle soft-tissue releases to alleviate joint restrictions. We pair these treatments with manageable posture adjustments so you can sit at your screen without constantly elevating your shoulders.

LOWER BACK

Lower Back and Hip Stiffness

Prolonged sitting locks the hips in flexion and flattens the natural lordotic curve of the lumbar spine, transferring continuous hydrostatic pressure onto the lower lumbar discs and surrounding ligaments. Many office workers notice an ache when rising from their desk chair at the end of the day or when bending down to tie their shoes. We evaluate pelvic alignment, hip mobility, and lumbar spine mechanics, utilizing specific adjustments to restore fluid movement to stiff spinal joints and relieve accumulated mechanical fatigue across the lower back.

HEADACHES & JAW

Headaches and Jaw Tension

Tension-type headaches and clenching of the jaw frequently accompany long stretches of concentrated desk work. Forward head posture can irritate the suboccipital nerves at the base of the skull, referring dull pressure behind the eyes, across the forehead, or around the temples. Furthermore, subconscious stress often manifests as clenching in the temporomandibular joints. We address these patterns by restoring gentle motion to the upper cervical joints, releasing tight suboccipital musculature, and providing practical guidance on jaw relaxation during high-focus working sessions.

ALSO SEEN

Mid-Back Stiffness, Forearm Strain, and Sciatica

We also frequently see mid-back stiffness between the shoulder blades, wrist and forearm strain from keyboard use, and sciatica-type leg discomfort linked to piriformis tension or lumbar disc irritation. Our team takes time to assess the root mechanism behind your symptoms. If an examination suggests nerve root compression or soft-tissue distress that falls within our scope, we provide gentle joint adjustments, myofascial releases, and nerve gliding exercises. However, we refer when it is not for us, directing patients promptly to specialized medical practitioners whenever findings warrant further evaluation.

When to See a Physician First

Certain symptoms require immediate medical assessment rather than chiropractic care. If you experience sudden muscle weakness in an arm or leg, numbness in the saddle area around your groin, unexplained changes in bowel or bladder function, high fever accompanying spinal pain, or back pain following traumatic injury, please consult a medical physician or visit an emergency department promptly. We maintain strict red-flag screening protocols during every initial consultation to ensure that every patient in our clinic receives safe, appropriate, and medically responsible care.

pages.title: Treatments and Care Methods
pages.content:
Treatments and Care Methods

Our clinical treatments combine precise spinal adjustments, targeted soft-tissue therapy, movement coaching, and workstation evaluations.

TREATMENTS

Chiropractic Adjustment

A chiropractic adjustment is a precise, low-amplitude manual impulse applied to a specific spinal or extremity joint that has lost its normal mobility. By gently restoring movement to restricted joint segments, adjustments reduce mechanical strain on nearby nerves and surrounding spinal musculature. Treatment is performed calmly on our padded tables, with clinicians explaining each step before applying any manual force. Most patients experience an immediate sensation of lightness and improved ease of rotation through the neck or spine.

Follow-up adjustment30 min$75

Adjustment and Soft-Tissue Work

When spinal joint restrictions are accompanied by chronic muscular hypertonicity, combining a joint adjustment with focused soft-tissue therapy provides deeper, longer-lasting relief. During these forty-five-minute appointments, our clinicians address stubborn trigger points in the trapezius, levator scapulae, piriformis, or lumbar paraspinal muscles before performing joint mobilization. Releasing taut muscle bands allows the spinal adjustment to take hold more comfortably, helping desk workers unburden their posture and maintain fluid joint mechanics through demanding workweeks.

Adjustment + soft-tissue work45 min$95

TREATMENT 03

Movement Plan Session

Passive hands-on treatment works best when reinforced by active spinal control. In our dedicated movement room, our kinesiologist evaluates your functional movement patterns, spinal articulation, and core bracing strategies. We identify compensations developed from sitting all day and teach you targeted, repeatable drills to restore hip extension, thoracic rotation, and shoulder stabilization. You receive a clear, personalized exercise program using simple tools like dowels or light resistance bands that can be completed at home or between office tasks.
Movement plan session · 45 min · $85

Book a first visit

TREATMENT 04

Desk and Posture Review

Pain that returns every Monday afternoon is often driven by an unsupportive desk set-up. For this specialized appointment, we ask you to bring photos or measurements of your current workspace, including chair height, monitor elevation, keyboard placement, and lighting. We analyze your sitting posture in detail, identifying ergonomic flaws that force your neck into excessive flexion or round your shoulders. We provide clear, practical recommendations for chair adjustments, display risers, and micro-breaks tailored to your daily schedule.
Desk & posture review (bring photos of your set-up) · 30 min · $60

Book a first visit

pages.content:
Your First Visit

We reserve a full sixty minutes for your initial appointment, ensuring ample time to listen, assess your movement, and begin care.

FIRST VISIT

The Four Stages of Your First Hour

Your initial sixty-minute visit is divided into four distinct, unhurried stages.

01

Talk

We sit down over tea or water to review your health history, work routine, and specific concerns.

15 min

02

A comprehensive posture and movement assessment evaluating spinal ranges of motion and joint mobility.

15 min

First adjustment

We provide gentle, appropriate manual therapy only if clinically indicated.

20 min

04

Plan

We outline practical home advice and discuss your recommended care schedule.

10 min

First visit fee60 min$120

FIRST VISIT

Preparing for Your Visit: Forms and Clothing

To make the most of your sixty minutes in Suite 204, please complete our online intake forms prior to your arrival, or come ten minutes early to fill them out at reception. We recommend wearing comfortable, flexible clothing such as gym wear, loose trousers, or a plain T-shirt so that you can move freely during the movement examination. If you are coming straight from the office, we have private changing space available. Please bring a list of any current medications and details of your extended health plan if you require formal reimbursement receipts.

What Happens Next: Follow-Up Rhythm

Healing accumulated postural fatigue takes steady, deliberate repetition. Following your initial consultation, we generally recommend weekly 30-minute follow-ups for 3 to 4 weeks to stabilize joint motion and reduce muscular hypertonicity. Once acute spinal restrictions subside and your comfort improves, appointments are spaced out to fortnightly or monthly check-ins based on your workload and personal goals. We continually re-evaluate your progress at each visit, ensuring your treatment schedule matches your real-world recovery rather than an arbitrary predetermined timetable. You remain in complete control of your care at every step.

Fees and Payment

We believe in straightforward, transparent pricing with no hidden costs, long prepaid commitments, or unexpected clinical charges.

FEES

FEES

Prices in CAD, tax included

All fees at Shisei Clinic are listed in CAD with applicable taxes included. Our pricing schedule is transparent and consistent across all clinicians.

Our five-visit package offers modest savings for patients undergoing initial weekly care, with a clear four-month validity period and no continuous renewal pressure.

Extended Health Plans, Cancellations, and Payment Methods

Most Canadian extended health insurance plans provide partial or full coverage for licensed chiropractic care, registered massage therapy, and kinesiology. We issue detailed itemized receipts upon payment that you can submit directly to your private insurer for prompt reimbursement. We accept Visa, Mastercard, Interac debit, and cash. Please note that our clinic maintains a firm 24-hour cancellation policy. If you need to reschedule or cancel an appointment, please notify us at least twenty-four hours in advance so we can offer that reserved clinical time to another patient awaiting treatment.

Our Clinicians and Team

Our team of seven dedicated professionals brings together chiropractic care, kinesiology, registered massage therapy, and clinic coordination.

CLINICIANS

THE TEAM

Seven people, one calm room

Dr. Naomi Hartley, DC

Founder & Clinic Director

Dr. Naomi Hartley founded Shisei Clinic in 2015 after seeing how forty hours of weekly computer use affected desk workers across Vancouver. A graduate with extensive clinical experience in spinal biomechanics, Dr. Hartley focuses on gentle thoracic and cervical adjustments paired with ergonomic education. She established our unhurried sixty-minute first-visit standard to ensure every patient receives thorough, compassionate assessment and clear guidance.

Dr. Tomás Reyes, DC & Dr. Priya Raman, DC

Chiropractors

Dr. Tomás Reyes and Dr. Priya Raman bring meticulous attention to joint mechanics and spinal rehabilitation. Dr. Reyes specializes in managing chronic lower back stiffness, sacroiliac joint dysfunction, and hip immobility resulting from prolonged seated posture. Dr. Raman focuses particularly on cervicogenic headaches, jaw clenching, and postural neck strain. Both chiropractors emphasize patient education, helping you understand how joint restrictions develop and how specific manual adjustments restore natural, pain-free range of motion during demanding work schedules.

Samuel Osei & Lena Vogel

Movement and Soft-Tissue Care

Samuel Osei is our staff kinesiologist who leads active rehabilitation in our dedicated movement room. Samuel designs progressive movement plans that rebuild hip mobility, thoracic extension, and postural endurance for office workers. Lena Vogel is our registered massage therapist, focusing on clinical deep tissue work, myofascial trigger point release, and targeted muscle unwinding. Working closely alongside our chiropractors, Samuel and Lena help ensure that muscular balance supports lasting spinal alignment and functional comfort throughout the working week.

Mei-Lin Chou & Claire Dubois

Reception and Clinic Operations

Mei-Lin Chou manages our front desk and handles patient bookings, welcoming you to Suite 204 with quiet efficiency and answering all questions regarding appointment preparation and insurance receipts. Claire Dubois is our clinic manager, overseeing our operations, facility standards, and patient communication. Together, Mei-Lin and Claire maintain the calm, organized environment that makes every visit to Shisei Clinic a restorative and seamless experience from the moment you step through our doors.

pages.title: Patient Stories
pages.content:
Patient Stories

Real accounts from desk workers who found relief from persistent postural fatigue through consistent, unhurried clinical care.

STORIES

STORIES

Three ordinary weeks

Product Designer

Ana Costa, 34

Ana Costa spends long stretches in front of dual monitors designing digital software interfaces, often working nine-hour screen days without significant movement breaks. By mid-week, she frequently experienced intense stiffness at the base of her skull and dull tension headaches that made concentrating difficult. During her sixty-minute initial consultation at Shisei Clinic, we identified restricted upper cervical joint motion and pronounced forward head carriage. Following an initial four-week course of gentle cervical adjustments combined with targeted suboccipital soft-tissue releases, Ana reports that her tension headaches have substantially reduced in frequency. She also adjusted her monitor height according to our recommendations and now incorporates brief doorway chest stretches between design sprints. Ana reports feeling noticeably clearer and more at ease during long afternoons at her desk.

Accountant

Marcus Bell, 51

Marcus Bell dreads every spring tax season, when seventy-hour weeks hunched over financial spreadsheets leave his lower back feeling locked, aching, and exhausted. By the end of March, rising from his chair had become an uncomfortable ordeal that left him stiff for several minutes. Marcus came to Shisei Clinic seeking relief from this recurrent seasonal pattern. Our assessment revealed limited hip extension and restricted mobility through his lower lumbar facets and sacroiliac joints. Over a series of thirty-minute follow-up adjustments paired with hip flexor mobility drills designed by our kinesiologist, Marcus found that his lower back felt progressively looser and more resilient. He reports being able to rise from his desk chair without hesitating, and he continues to visit monthly for maintenance care to keep his spine moving freely.

Translator

Ingrid Halvorsen, 42

Ingrid Halvorsen works from a home studio translating literary and technical texts, spending hours maintaining intense concentration while typing. Over several years, she noticed persistent tightness elevating her shoulders, accompanied by constant nocturnal clenching of her jaw that left her facial muscles tender each morning. At Shisei Clinic, we combined gentle thoracic spinal adjustments with focused soft-tissue therapy to relax hypertonic shoulder and neck musculature. We also reviewed her keyboard setup and provided simple relaxation drills for her temporomandibular joints. Ingrid reports that her jaw clenching has eased considerably and that her shoulders rest in a much more natural, lowered position while typing. She found that the calm rhythm of her treatments helped her become far more aware of tension before it accumulated into severe pain.

Questions first? Call +1 604 555 0142 or write to hello@shisei.example. Reception is open six days a week.

pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.content:
Frequently Asked Questions

Clear answers to common questions about our chiropractic care, clinical methods, appointment preparation, and fees.

QUESTIONS

QUESTIONS

Before a first visit

What should I wear to my first appointment?

We recommend wearing comfortable, loose-fitting clothing that allows you to move freely, such as gym trousers, leggings, sweatpants, or a soft cotton T-shirt. During the movement and posture examination, our clinicians will ask you to perform simple standing and seated movements so we can evaluate spinal mobility. If you are arriving directly from your office in business attire, we provide a private changing space in Suite 204 where you can change into more comfortable clothing before your appointment begins.

Do you take X-rays before adjusting?

No, we do not take routine X-rays in our clinic. Current clinical guidelines demonstrate that routine spinal imaging is rarely necessary for uncomplicated mechanical back pain, neck stiffness, or desk-related postural fatigue. We conduct a thorough physical examination and orthopaedic assessment during your sixty-minute first visit. Diagnostic imaging is only recommended when examination reveals specific neurological signs, trauma, or clinical red flags. In those rare situations, we promptly refer you to a medical physician or specialized imaging facility.

Do I need to sign up for a long prepaid package?

Absolutely not. We never ask our patients to commit to high-volume prepaid treatment packages, and we do not pressure anyone into long-term financial agreements. We offer a simple five-visit follow-up package for $340 CAD that provides a modest discount for patients undergoing an initial block of care, valid for four months. Beyond that, you are always free to pay on a visit-by-visit basis. We recommend appointment intervals based strictly on your individual recovery and clinical needs.

Can I claim visits under my extended health plan?

Yes. Most Canadian extended health insurance policies provide reimbursement coverage for licensed chiropractic care, registered massage therapy, and kinesiology sessions. After each visit, our reception team provides a comprehensive, itemized receipt containing your practitioner's registration number, date of service, and exact treatment code. You can easily submit these receipts through your insurer's online portal or mobile application for prompt direct reimbursement according to your policy limits.

What is the difference between a first visit and a follow-up?

Your first visit is a comprehensive sixty-minute appointment divided into four clear stages: fifteen minutes of discussion regarding your health history and work habits, fifteen minutes of postural and movement examination, twenty minutes for your initial adjustment if appropriate, and ten minutes to establish a personalized care plan. Follow-up appointments last thirty minutes and focus directly on evaluating your progress, performing targeted spinal adjustments, and fine-tuning your home exercises.

Does a chiropractic adjustment hurt?

Chiropractic adjustments are generally very gentle and should not cause sharp pain. Our practitioners use precise, controlled manual techniques tailored to your body type and comfort level. You may occasionally hear a light popping or clicking sound, which is simply the natural release of gas bubbles from within the synovial joint fluid. Most patients report an immediate sense of tension release and improved mobility. Some mild, temporary muscular soreness similar to starting a new exercise routine can occasionally occur.

How many visits will I need before I feel better?

Every individual responds differently based on how long their postural strain has been developing and how demanding their weekly desk routine remains. Many patients report initial symptom relief within two to four treatments. We typically suggest weekly thirty-minute appointments for three to four weeks to stabilize spinal joint mechanics and relieve muscle hypertonicity. After that initial phase, we re-evaluate your progress together and space appointments out to fortnightly or monthly maintenance visits depending on your preferences.

What happens if chiropractic care is not right for my condition?

We practice with clear clinical boundaries and believe strongly in collaborative healthcare. During your initial consultation, we conduct thorough orthopaedic and neurological screening tests. If your symptoms suggest underlying pathology, acute disc herniation with progressive nerve deficit, systemic inflammatory conditions, or other medical issues outside our scope of practice, we will inform you clearly. We will refer you directly to a family physician, medical specialist, or imaging clinic to ensure you receive the appropriate care.

How far in advance do I need to cancel or reschedule?

We require a minimum of twenty-four hours notice for all appointment cancellations or rescheduling requests. Because our practitioners reserve dedicated thirty-minute and sixty-minute time blocks for each patient, adequate notice allows us to offer open slots to individuals waiting for care. Cancellations made with less than twenty-four hours notice may be subject to a missed appointment fee. You can easily adjust your booking by calling our reception desk at +1 604 555 0142 or emailing hello@shisei.example.

Can I combine chiropractic adjustments with massage or movement coaching?

Yes, combining therapies is often an effective way to address persistent desk fatigue. While a chiropractic adjustment restores fluid movement to restricted spinal joints, registered massage therapy releases hypertonic muscle tissue, and kinesiology sessions build postural endurance and movement control. You can book forty-five-minute joint and soft-tissue treatments with our chiropractors, or schedule separate sessions with our registered massage therapist Lena Vogel or our kinesiologist Samuel Osei to support comprehensive, long-term spinal health.

Questions first? Call +1 604 555 0142 or write to hello@shisei.example. Reception is open six days a week.

posts.title: Sitting is not the enemy; staying still is
posts.excerpt: Postural fatigue at the desk rarely stems from sitting itself, but rather from maintaining a single static position for hours without movement.
posts.content:
Over the past decade, office workers have been told repeatedly that sitting is inherently hazardous to human health. Standing desks, ergonomic balls, and kneeling chairs have proliferated across Vancouver offices, often accompanied by the anxiety that every hour spent in a chair damages the spine. Yet in our treatment rooms at Shisei Clinic, we see people who stand all day experiencing just as much spinal discomfort as those who sit. The underlying problem is rarely the chair itself. The real culprit is staying completely still for forty hours a week.

The human spine is a remarkably resilient structure composed of thirty-three vertebrae, interconnected by flexible facet joints, strong ligaments, and fluid-filled intervertebral discs. These spinal structures rely entirely on movement to maintain their health. Unlike muscles, which receive a direct and continuous blood supply from capillaries, spinal discs depend on mechanical compression and decompression—a natural pumping action created by walking, bending, twisting, and shifting—to draw in nutrients and flush out metabolic waste products. When you remain frozen in one upright posture for hours while concentrating on a screen, this fluid circulation diminishes, leaving joint tissues stiff and fatigued.

Many people attempt to correct their posture by forcing themselves into a rigid, military-style upright position. They pull their shoulders back, push their chest out, and lock their lower back in an exaggerated arch. While this posture may look attentive, maintaining it requires continuous, isometric muscular contraction. Within thirty minutes, the muscles of the mid-back and neck become exhausted, leading to deep, burning tension. Rigid posture is simply another form of staying still. A healthy posture is not a frozen position that you hold with continuous effort; it is a dynamic posture that shifts, relaxes, and breathes throughout the workday.

Instead of fighting your chair or obsessing over perfect alignment, the most effective strategy is to introduce micro-movements into your working hours. Shift your weight from one hip to the other every ten minutes. Lean back against your chair's backrest during phone calls to let your spinal erectors rest. Stand up and walk across the room while reading a brief document. Reach both arms toward the ceiling between scheduled meetings to open the ribcage and encourage thoracic extension. These brief, effortless movements rehydrate your spinal discs and prevent the accumulation of static pressure.

When joints do become restricted from weeks of prolonged immobility, chiropractic care helps restore normal segmental movement that you cannot easily unlock on your own. During a thirty-minute follow-up at our Linden Row clinic, we identify specific vertebral segments that have lost their fluid motion and apply gentle, precise adjustments to restore joint glide. Combined with simple home mobility drills, this care allows your body to adapt comfortably to the realities of modern computer work without chronic strain. Sitting is an unavoidable part of working life, but your body was built to move within it.
